Attached is the working MAP (MAP-v3.xlsx) and the benchmark script bundle we plan to run. This thread will capture run scheduling, access, and acceptance criteria so we can close the PO on the timeline we discussed. High level plan below: 

- Objective: Validate production-like latency and throughput for your core inference endpoint under your anticipated concurrency (target: 32 and 64 concurrent clients).
- Primary metrics: p50/p95 latency (ms), throughput (req/s), TTFT (time-to-first-token) for 1k token prompts, CPU/GPU utilization and error rate.
- Test env: Staging-2 in us-west (identical model pin 1.2.0).
- Access needed: service account + API key for staging, 2 test user accounts, and a test S3 bucket for artifacts.
- Windows: two 3-hour windows (Wed 17 Mar 10:00–13:00 PT — exploratory, Tue 22 Mar 08:30–11:30 PT — acceptance run).

Please confirm the windows and the contact for network/VPN access. Karthik — can you confirm the exact model variant we will route to and whether KV cache will be enabled for the runs?

Thanks,
Sean

Subject: RE: MAP draft: performance plan + access checklist for OpenEdge — results and next steps

David/Priya — thanks for running with us today. Quick summary of the acceptance window (artifacts attached: bench-results-20270322.csv, run-summary-20270322.pdf):

- Environment: Staging-2 (redwood/open-l2-1.2.0-fp16), KV cache ON, sequence length 1024 pinned.
- Concurrency tested: 32 and 64 parallel clients.
- Throughput: 32 conc -> steady 220 req/s; 64 conc -> steady 410 req/s (averaged over 45 min steady-state).
- Latency (request-origin -> first token):
  - 32 conc: p50 = 78 ms, p95 = 210 ms
  - 64 conc: p50 = 115 ms, p95 = 380 ms
- TTFT (1k token prompts, request-origin):
  - 32 conc: median TTFT = 420 ms
  - 64 conc: median TTFT = 670 ms
- Errors: <0.3% total (transient 429s during short burst; we validated backpressure behavior).
- Resource notes: GPU utilization ~78% at 64 conc; no GPU OOMs; CPU spikes correlated with simultaneous artifact write.

Acceptance: Based on the MAP acceptance criteria in MAP-v3.xlsx, OpenEdge passes the performance targets for 32 concurrent clients and is within tolerance for 64 with recommendation to enable a lightweight prefix caching layer in production to reduce p95 further.

Next steps: 
- Redwood to provide a short SRE runbook for production rollout (eta 5 working days).
- OpenEdge to confirm go/no-go for Dedicated capacity or staged host routing.
- Sign-off: please reply with a short confirmation and we'll attach the MAP closure to the PO.

Thanks again — detailed CSV attached for your analytics. Happy to jump on a call tomorrow to review graphs.

Best,
Sean
